A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The complete main texts and appendices A–I support comparison, with retained material identifiable despite renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original diffusion-training experiments on Gaussian and image datasets, including generated-sample covariance trajectories and spectral-scaling analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds patch-convolution simulations and CNN architecture ablations.

M1.justification: The analytical framework, denoiser parameterizations, training objectives, and sampling procedures remain unchanged. The new CNN-ResNet serves as an experimental ablation model rather than a revision of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Gaussian, point-cloud, MNIST, CIFAR-10, FFHQ, and AFHQ coverage is retained. The added experiments use existing FFHQ32 coverage; high-channel latent representations are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: No competing baseline is added or removed. The new CNN-ResNet configurations investigate architectural effects rather than introduce a competing method evaluated against the analytical framework.

E3.justification: v3 adds controlled CNN-ResNet experiments varying depth and channels, with 50,000 training steps and 2,000 evaluation samples (I.7). It also introduces patch-convolution simulations varying filter sizes from 3 to 25 and initialization (B.1.2). These substantially extend the evaluation design; existing experiment protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses investigate how patch size and initialization affect spectral scaling (B.1.2), and how CNN width and depth affect convergence and spectral ordering (B.2.4). They directly probe the previously unresolved discrepancy between linear theory and practical convolutional networks.

E5.justification: Fit-quality and mode-count reporting continue without new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The fixed-noise visualization is retained.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports increasing-mode scaling exponents ranging from +0.48 at patch size 3 to −0.30 at size 25. Figures 22–26 add findings that wider CNNs converge faster with weaker spectral ordering. Existing results, including the FFHQ32 MLP exponents −0.48 and −0.35, are retained.

T1.justification: v3 corrects covariance reconstruction in C.5, convolutional initial conditions and missing factors in G.3–G.4, and the orthogonality assumption and 4η-to-8η coefficients in H.3. The principal theoretical framework remains intact. However, D.1.1 introduces erroneous transpose symbols in place of iteration exponents in Eqs. 78–80.

C1.justification: The abstract and main contributions retain the same claims: analytical distribution dynamics, inverse-variance spectral ordering, validation in MLPs, and distinct convolutional learning behavior. New evidence supports and interprets these existing claims.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2, 6.2, and 7 substantially expand the explanation of convolutional departures through patch size, initialization, and network width. v3 hypothesizes a role for width relative to input channels and discusses implications for high-channel representations. Figure 18 also newly qualifies patch-level spectral bias as not always robust.

D1.justification: Appendix I.7 documents the new ResNet architecture, depth/channel choices, Adam optimizer, learning rate, training budget, evaluation sample count, and absence of attention and augmentation. B.1.2 explains the numerical simulation procedure. Existing implementation, hardware, and code-access disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Five references are added: latent diffusion, deep compression autoencoders, representation autoencoders, empirical Bayes/Tweedie's formula, and the I-MMSE relationship. They support new applicability discussion and mathematical explanations; the main related-work positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits appendix prose, clarifies derivation headings and transitions, and locally reorders the distribution/asymptotics discussion in E.2. It also adds acknowledgements and conference information. These refinements retain the overall narrative and appendix organization.

P2.justification: v3 adds architecture schematics to Table 1, a new Table 2, and six figures: 7 and 22–26. Appendix equations are extensively regrouped and realigned, alongside caption and hyperlink-format changes. Existing figure artwork is retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new convolutional simulations and controlled architecture ablations strengthen the previously largely speculative explanation of departures from spectral ordering. Added experimental details and several mathematical corrections improve clarity and support. These gains outweigh localized regressions, particularly the erroneous iteration exponents in D.1.1, but do not resolve the broader absence of a complete theory for practical CNNs.
